newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan one-month NCDs average yield at 6.188 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan one-month NCDs average yield at 6.188 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank on Friday issued T$3 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposits at an average yield of 6.188 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the yields was between 6.050 percent and 6.250 percent. Demand totalled T$3.5 billion.
The central bank's recent non-stop NCD issuance was seen widely in the market as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
Taiwan's deputy central bank governor Liang Cheng-chin on Wednesday flatly denied that this was the case, saying the bank was acting purely in response to the liquidity situation.

"The scale of the central bank's NCD issuance was determined by the liquidity situation. It has no direct or close relation with the stock market's movements," Liang said after Wednesday's market close.
"It (the bank) will not issue more and fewer NCDs simply because the stock market rises or falls," Liang said.
Liang said banking system's liquidity remains fairly loose, prompting the central bank to mop up excess funds.
On Friday, the island's benchmark stock index fell 262.6 points, or 3.09 percent, to close at 8,230.07 dampened by an export ban on fresh and frozen pork, brokers said.
The government's latest attempt to cool down the overheated market also triggered heavy selling, they said.
